{"id": "29:58/q05", "question": "How does the lodging verb govern غرفا?", "turns_on": "Whether غرفا is the b-w-ʾ verb's second object, or how the th-w-y form licenses an accusative place despite objections to athwaytuhu al-dār.", "positions": [{"id": "29:58/q05/p1", "position": "غرفا is the second object of the b-w-ʾ verb, with the believers as its first object.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Samīn state this; al-Samīn cites 3:121 and the lām construction in 22:26. Al-Ālūsī gives this analysis of the chambers. Abū Ḥayyān gives direct-object analysis as an option."}, {"id": "29:58/q05/p4", "position": "غرفا may be a locative accusative, treating a specified place as an unmarked location.", "reasons": "Al-Fārisī says a preposition can be omitted before a specific location; al-Wāḥidī records Abū ʿAlī's road, Syria, and lavatory examples. {"id": "29:58/q06", "question": "Is there a different vowel reading of غرفا?", "turns_on": "The vowel on the rāʾ of the plural غرفا.", "positions": [{"id": "29:58/q06/p1", "position": "The usual form has the ordinary vowel on the rāʾ.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya contrasts Ibn ʿĀmir's ḍamma-vowel form with the other reading; Abū Ḥayyān and al-Ālūsī likewise identify his variant."}, {"id": "29:58/q06/p2", "position": "Ibn ʿĀmir reads the rāʾ with ḍamma, ghurufan.", "reasons": "Reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū Ḥayyān, and al-Ālūsī."}]}
{"id": "29:58/q07", "question": "What are the promised غرف?", "turns_on": "Whether the notes describe the chambers by elevation, precious materials, or the transmitted transparency and visible ranks; these descriptions are not presented as mutually exclusive.", "positions": [{"id": "29:58/q07/p1", "position": "Lofty upper chambers or palaces in Paradise.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī says chambers stand above ordinary houses and offer cleaner air and a more pleasant, dry dwelling; al-Rāzī takes their height to signify believers' exalted rank (39:20). Ibn Kathīr says the inhabitants direct the rivers as they wish."}, {"id": "29:58/q07/p2", "position": "Palaces or chambers made of pearl, emerald or beryl, and ruby.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī and al-Ṭabrisī transmit this from Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Ālūsī transmits pearl, beryl, and ruby from him. Bursevī gives pearl, emerald, and ruby."}, {"id": "29:58/q07/p3", "position": "Transparent rooms whose inside and outside can be seen through each other.", "reasons": "Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits the Prophet's description; al-Māwardī cites Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, al-Qurṭubī cites al-Tirmidhī from ʿAlī, and Ibn Kathīr and Study Quran repeat the report. {"id": "29:58/q09", "question": "Where do the rivers flow beneath the rooms?", "turns_on": "What the pronoun and the description 'beneath' locate: the chambers or garden trees.", "positions": [{"id": "29:58/q09/p1", "position": "Beneath the chambers themselves.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās locates them beneath the chambers and relates their water to 47:15. {"id": "29:58/q13", "question": "What does فيها refer to, and how is خالدين parsed?", "turns_on": "Whether the feminine pronoun resumes the chambers or Paradise.", "positions": [{"id": "29:58/q13/p1", "position": "فيها refers to the chambers; خالدين is an accusative circumstance of the verb's pronoun.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī allows the chambers as antecedent. {"id": "29:59/q02", "question": "Who are those described as patient and reliant?", "turns_on": "Whether the description is stated broadly of believing workers or applied particularly to persecuted migrants.", "positions": [{"id": "29:59/q02/p1", "position": "They are the believing workers promised reward, especially believers enduring persecution and migration.", "reasons": "Yaḥyā ibn Sallām and al-Thaʿlabī identify the praised people as patient believers who rely on God. {"id": "29:59/q03", "question": "What does their patience involve?", "turns_on": "Whether patience is described by its religious acts and hardships, by its kinds or acknowledgment, or by one's inward reception of affliction.", "positions": [{"id": "29:59/q03/p1", "position": "Steadfastness through religious hardship, including persecution, migration, privation, obedience, and restraint from sin.", "reasons": "Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, reported by Ibn Abī Ḥātim, specifies perseverance in God's command. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Nasafī, Abū Ḥayyān, and al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī include obedience and avoiding sin or desires; al-Nasafī also lists leaving home, polytheists, trials, and calamities. {"id": "29:59/q06", "question": "When should believers endure harm where they are, and when should they migrate?", "turns_on": "Whether the distinction is the believer's ability to migrate or ability to practice religion in the present land.", "positions": [{"id": "29:59/q06/p1", "position": "Those able to leave a harmful place should migrate and rely on God; those unable should endure and continue worship.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī reads the surrounding exhortation, including 29:56, as addressing these two groups according to their ability to depart."}, {"id": "29:59/q06/p2", "position": "Endure harm while religious practice remains possible; migrate and endure migration's hardship when it becomes impossible.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī makes ability to practice religion in one's land the criterion for staying or leaving."}]}
{"id": "29:59/q07", "question": "How does this verse connect to the surrounding passage?", "turns_on": "Which surrounding theme supplies the connection: migrants' provision, the promised reward, or the contrast with impatient disbelievers.", "positions": [{"id": "29:59/q07/p1", "position": "It reassures migrants who feared losing home and livelihood that God will provide.", "reasons": "Muqātil says migrants lacking money or livelihood in Medina were admonished to take heed. {"id": "29:59/q08", "question": "What reports are cited about reward for the faithful in this passage?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "29:59/q08/p1", "position": "The Prophet describes transparent chambers prepared for people who feed others, speak well, fast, and pray while others sleep.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr reports this prophetic statement through Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī in connection with the promised chambers."}, {"id": "29:59/q08/p2", "position": "A person who flees even a short distance with his religion merits Paradise and companionship with Abraham and Muhammad.", "reasons": "Al-Bursawī cites the hadith and explains Paradise as recompense for giving up home for religion, and their companionship as recompense for following their migration and reviving their practice."}]}
{"id": "29:59/q09", "question": "What can migration mean for the spiritual traveler?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "29:59/q09/p1", "position": "Leaving social prestige and public acceptance for obscurity.", "reasons": "Al-Bursawī gives this inward sense. {"id": "3:200/q01", "question": "What does 'be patient' require?", "turns_on": "Whether general obedience or a specific setting defines the command.", "positions": [{"id": "3:200/q01/p1", "position": "Steadfastness in religion and obedience, including duties, abstaining from sin and trials.", "reasons": "Tabari favors unrestricted scope because God specified no exception. {"id": "3:200/q12", "question": "How does the closing verse connect to the sūra and its neighbors?", "turns_on": "Immediate summary, inter-sūra link or wider sūra context.", "positions": [{"id": "3:200/q12/p1", "position": "It gathers beliefs and duties, renewing resolve after Uhud.", "reasons": "Razi lists monotheism, justice, prophecy, resurrection, pilgrimage and jihad; Asamm connects many duties. {"id": "3:200/q14", "question": "What virtues and recitations of Āl ʿImrān are reported?", "turns_on": "Reports differ in reward and Friday timing; Alusi rejects the bridge report.", "positions": [{"id": "3:200/q14/p1", "position": "Friday recitation wins divine and angelic blessings until sunset or sunrise.", "reasons": "Kashshaf and Alusi give sunset; Baydawi gives sunrise."}, {"id": "3:200/q14/p2", "position": "The two radiant sūras plead for reciters at Judgment.", "reasons": "Nasafi and Study Quran describe clouds, sunrays or birds interceding."}, {"id": "3:200/q14/p3", "position": "Each recited verse grants safety on the bridge over Hell.", "reasons": "Kashshaf and Baydawi transmit it; Alusi calls it fabricated and censures transmitters."}, {"id": "3:200/q14/p4", "position": "Reciting the ending at night earns vigil reward; the Prophet recited its final ten at night.", "reasons": "Alusi transmits Uthman and Abu Hurayra; Kur'an Yolu reports tahajjud practice."}]}

{"id": "3:200/q17", "question": "Why does the verse address believers as a collective?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:200/q17/p1", "position": "Human life is intrinsically social, and revelation consciously organizes shared religious life.", "reasons": "Tabatabai traces marriage and household into clan and rule through strength, wealth and political skill; this early hierarchy encouraged idolatry. {"id": "3:200/q22", "question": "How should the Muslim community govern and maintain its bonds?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "3:200/q22/p1", "position": "It shares responsibility under prophetic guidance, consultation, faith-based belonging and collective duty.", "reasons": "Tabatabai cites Prophetic authority (64:12; 4:105; 33:6; 3:31) and general commands to believers, while the Prophet uniquely teaches and purifies (62:2). {"id": "30:60/q01", "question": "What patience does the Prophet's command require?", "turns_on": "The explanations emphasize different objects and practices of patience: hostile conduct, continued proclamation, restraint from haste, or the inner experience of affliction.", "positions": [{"id": "30:60/q01/p1", "position": "Endure the opponents' rejection, abuse, and obstinacy while trusting the promised outcome.", "reasons": "Yaḥyā ties endurance to victory and the religion's triumph; al-Ṭabarī adds bearing abuse and delivering the message, with establishment for the Prophet and followers in the land. Al-Wāḥidī, Ibn Kathīr, al-Biqāʿī, al-Ālūsī, and Ibn ʿĀshūr connect patience to rejection after sealed hearts or persistent unbelief; al-Biqāʿī says even hostility falls within God's will.
